concepts.heading: Making AI enrichment efficient
concepts.body: Pre-filter AI steps deterministically to eligible rows, for example rows with a non-empty note that changed since the last run, and leave the rest null. Process incrementally and cache results on normalized input content and prompt version, calling the model only on cache misses. These measures usually cut cost far more than switching models. When an AI step's quality metric changes suddenly, treat it as an incident: sample outputs, compare model and prompt versions and inputs with the previous run, hold affected rows, fix and backfill.

concepts.heading: Reviewing AI-generated code and outputs
concepts.body: The exam guide asks data engineers to review AI-generated code and outputs for incorrect assumptions, unsupported patterns and regressions, exactly like a teammate's change. Look for scale-unsafe patterns such as collecting a distributed dataset to one node, redundant computation, implicit `SELECT *` that couples the output to the input's full schema, hard-coded reference lists, missed incremental opportunities, and changed join types or filters that alter semantics. Reject generated logic that fills curated business values with statistical guesses such as mean imputation. Passing generated unit tests is not enough, since they cover only the cases the assistant imagined; a branch build compared with production by key is the evidence of equivalence. Generated expectations and data models are drafts to verify against the real contract and data.

examPoints: When a scenario asks where AI should run, prefer the pipeline for reusable, row-wise enrichment stored as properties, and the application or Ontology layer for on-demand reasoning in a user's context.

When a scenario presents AI-generated transforms that build successfully, prefer review against the contract plus a branch comparison with production over merging on a green build or passing generated tests.

quiz.q: Support agents want every ticket routed by category as it arrives, and also want to ask ad hoc questions about a single ticket's history. How should the AI work be placed?
choices: Both tasks in the application, generated each time a user opens a ticket
Both tasks in a nightly pipeline, precomputing answers to every possible question
Category classification as a validated pipeline step stored as a property; ad hoc questions answered on demand at the application layer
Category classification by the AI engineer's agent; ad hoc questions by an LLM transform
quiz.explain: Reusable per-item results that drive routing belong in the pipeline, while context-dependent questions from a user belong at the application or Ontology layer.

quiz.q: Unit tests written by a code assistant all pass for its new transform, yet comparing a branch build with production shows a few thousand keys whose values differ. What should the engineer do?
choices: Merge, since the unit tests passed and the build succeeded
Delete the production output so that only the new version remains
Regenerate the transform until the differences disappear without inspecting them
Investigate the differences before merging, because the tests cover only the cases the assistant imagined
quiz.explain: Branch comparison on real data is the evidence of equivalence; unexplained differences must be understood before any merge.

days.recap: Run reusable AI enrichment in the pipeline and interactive reasoning at the application layer, stay within the data engineer's role, and review all AI-generated work with the same evidence demanded of human changes.

days.title: Final Review: Cross-Domain Judgement and Exam Readiness

concepts.heading: What the exam looks like
concepts.body: The Data Engineer – Associate exam is a timed, open-book, multiple-choice exam of 95 questions in 3 hours, with a pass mark of 70% correct, and certificates are valid for two years. It covers eight domains, from Data Connectivity and Ingestion to AI-Assisted Data Engineering. Palantir does not publish domain weights, so this bank weights the eight domains equally; do not assume any domain is safe to skip. After a failed attempt there is a 14-day wait before retaking. Budget a little under two minutes per question and avoid sinking too much time into any single scenario.

concepts.heading: The troubleshooting playbook across domains
concepts.body: Many questions in every domain test the same playbook: state the symptom precisely, find the first bad stage, separate data, code, permission and resource causes, assess blast radius, choose the smallest safe repair, verify and add a preventive control. Stale output with green builds points upstream to syncs; a sudden full recompute points to input transactions; a slow build points to a comparison with a fast one; an access failure points to Check Access. Answers that rebuild everything first, grant broad access, add resources blindly or silence a check are the distractors the exam guide warns against. Pick the option that gathers the right evidence before acting.

concepts.heading: Recurring "simplest safe option" patterns
concepts.body: The exam rewards the simplest option that meets the stated requirement: snapshot over CDC when the table is small, incremental over streaming when freshness is daily, a lightweight engine for small inputs, direct connections when the source is reachable. Safety comes from branches with output comparison, build-blocking expectations for real invariants, markings that follow data and least-privilege grants through groups. Distrust options that overwrite production, unmark data for convenience, fill gaps with guessed values or rely on a longer prompt or bigger model. Read every scenario for the real requirement before choosing.

concepts.heading: Role boundary and final checklist
concepts.body: Keep answers inside the data engineer's column: pipelines, ingestion, curated data, data quality, project structure and data security, Ontology data modeling and pipeline-layer AI. Agents, prompts and interactive AI belong to the AI engineer, and the user-facing query experience to the application layer, so options that make the data engineer own them are usually distractors. Before the exam, rehearse the four transaction types, the fallback triggers, the expectation-versus-health-check split, the access layers, stable keys and link cardinality, and pipeline-versus-application AI placement. Each is a short rule that unlocks many scenario questions.

examPoints: When a scenario offers both a quick broad fix (rebuild everything, grant Owner, add memory, remove the check) and a targeted evidence-based step, prefer the targeted step that finds the first bad stage.

When a scenario's options include work owned by another role, such as building the agent or the application, prefer the option that keeps the data engineer responsible for the data, pipeline and model that the other role depends on.

quiz.q: Which statement about the Data Engineer – Associate exam matches the published facts?
choices: It has 95 multiple-choice questions in 3 hours with a 70% pass mark, and domain weights are not published
It is a hands-on lab exam in a live Foundry environment with no multiple-choice questions
It has 65 questions in 90 minutes and weights the ingestion domain most heavily
It has no pass mark; candidates receive a percentile ranking only
quiz.explain: The official guide lists 95 questions, 3 hours, a 70% pass mark and eight domains without published weights; hands-on exams belong to the Specialist level.

quiz.q: An incremental pipeline's output is stale, its builds are green and an analyst suggests granting the pipeline Owner on every project "just in case". What is the best first step?
choices: Grant Owner as suggested, since it rules out permission problems
Find the first bad stage by checking the upstream sync and the input transactions since the last good run
Force a full rebuild of every downstream dataset immediately
Disable the freshness health check so that the alerts stop
quiz.explain: The playbook starts with evidence at the first bad stage; broad grants, blind rebuilds and silenced checks are the distractors the exam guide warns against.

days.recap: Across all eight domains, gather evidence before acting, choose the simplest safe option that meets the real requirement, and keep answers inside the data engineer's role.
